theme: When the important task waits for the trivial one
title: Per-Lock Protocol Assignment Against Priority Inversion
innovation_hook: Strict priority scheduling is correct in isolation and causes unbounded inversion when a low-priority task holds a lock. The insight is choosing between inheritance and ceiling protocols per resource based on the contention pattern.
strategies: no-protocol baseline: echo the checker's own construction (plain fixed-priority, no boosting on any lock) -> reproduces the baseline exactly, ~0.1

uniform priority-inheritance on every lock (the standard OS-course fix for priority inversion): fixes locks nobody proactively over-blocks but is unprotected during the early window before the real waiter arrives, so it loses badly on ceiling-favoring locks

exact per-lock search: simulate the same deterministic scheduler locally over every {none,inherit,ceiling}^L combination and keep the true minimum-cost assignment -- exploits the per-resource contention pattern directly instead of one global rule
